leftEvidence.title: Two blind men call Jesus Son of David

points.label: Action and response
points.left: The men follow Jesus crying for mercy, answer his question about belief, receive touch and sight, and spread the report despite a warning.
points.right: The woman cries for mercy and her daughter, meets silence and disciple pressure, debates lost sheep and household crumbs, is commended for faith, and her daughter is healed.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places Davidic address is joined to mercy, trust, healing, and uncontrolled report inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places a Davidic plea persists through boundary language until healing is announced inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Matthew 9:27–31 and Matthew 15:21–28 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Gospel and Apostolic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: A Canaanite woman calls the Son of David

payload.tension: Matthew 9:27–31 foregrounds Davidic address is joined to mercy, trust, healing, and uncontrolled report; Matthew 15:21–28 foregrounds a Davidic plea persists through boundary language until healing is announced. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
